study_identification_part.si4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To introduce spectral normative modeling (SNM), a novel method that leverages brain eigenmodes for efficient spatial reconstruction to generate normative ranges for arbitrary regions of interest at high spatial resolution, overcoming computational constraints and parcellation dependencies of conventional normative models.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons: Two-sample t-tests between HC and AD groups with nonparametric FDR correction (α=5%, 1000 permutations) to identify vertices with significant differences. Correlation analysis: Pearson correlation coefficients between vertex-wise z-scores and MMSE cognitive scores with nonparametric FDR correction via permutation testing (1000 permutations). Biomarker validation: Pearson correlation between ETVC and MMSE scores. Sensitivity analysis: ETVC computed across different z-score thresholds to assess predictive power. Within-group analyses: Correlations performed separately for HC, MCI, and AD cohorts. Interindividual heterogeneity: Euclidean distance matrix between deviation maps, multidimensional scaling (MDS) for 2D embedding, visualization of heterogeneity landscape.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: SNM achieved 98.3% speedup in computing normative ranges across spatial scales while maintaining accuracy comparable to conventional models. In the AD clinical application, SNM successfully replicated established cortical atrophy patterns and demonstrated that extreme thinning (ETVC) predicts cognitive impairment (r=-0.45, p<0.0001), with substantial heterogeneity in individual atrophy patterns.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Performance and efficiency: SNM with 1000 eigenmodes (~2% of total dimensionality) achieved performance matching direct normative models across all spatial scales (brain-wide, regional, and high-resolution). Training time was reduced from months to less than 2 days, and assessment time from minutes to seconds - a 98.3% computational speedup. Clinical findings: Group-level analysis revealed widespread cortical thinning in AD across temporal, parietal, and frontal lobes, with some abnormal thickening in visual areas (lingual gyrus, cuneus), replicating established findings. The ETVC biomarker showed strong association with cognitive impairment (r=-0.45, p<0.0001 in full sample; r=-0.31, p<0.0001 within AD cohort; no significant correlation in HC or MCI). Extreme atrophy (z between -3 and -2) contributed more to predictive power than mild atrophy. Heterogeneity analysis: AD individuals exhibited significantly greater variability in deviation patterns compared to HC and MCI groups. Multidimensional scaling revealed distinct subgroups characterized by negligible, localized, or widespread atrophy. Two AD individuals with similar demographics and diagnoses showed markedly different cortical thinning patterns (r=0.05, p_spin=0.24), highlighting substantial individual heterogeneity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: SNM enables multiple novel applications: 1) Atlas-free normative assessment - can generate normative estimates for any brain parcellation scheme without retraining; 2) Individualized parcellation - can assess patient-specific functional networks; 3) Transfer learning capability - demonstrated successful generalization to independent clinical site (MACC) with small fine-tuning sample (66 HC); 4) Privacy-preserving deployment - model parameters can be shared without original training data; 5) Federated learning potential - architecture suitable for training on decentralized datasets; 6) Native space projection - deviation maps can be overlaid onto individual's native brain space for clinical interpretation; 7) Heterogeneity mapping - enables continuous landscape analysis of individual deviations rather than discrete subtype classification; 8) Potential for multi-modal extension - framework applicable to other phenotypes (white matter microstructure, functional connectivity, metabolic measures). Code and fitted parameters will be made openly available.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1) Current model assumes Gaussian distributions and does not extend to phenotypes with substantial skewness or kurtosis, though future integration with likelihood warping techniques could address this. 2) The approach assumes adequate low-frequency eigenmode representation of the phenomenon; reconstruction accuracy tests are needed for different phenotypes and queries. 3) Evaluation used connectivity eigenmodes from random-walk Laplacian; other basis sets or shift operators may perform differently. 4) High-resolution lateralization queries showed reduced goodness of fit, possibly due to misaligned gyrification patterns between contralateral vertices. 5) Clinical findings are preliminary and require further studies for specific clinical applications (diagnosis, prognosis, differential diagnosis). 6) Current study limited to cortical surface; extension to volumetric space requires voxel-wise eigenmodes.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a methodological paper introducing a novel normative modeling framework rather than a traditional clinical study. Key innovation: Spectral Normative Modeling (SNM) leverages graph signal processing and brain connectivity eigenmodes to achieve computational efficiency and spatial versatility. The method represents a paradigm shift from conventional approaches by modeling normative ranges in a low-dimensional eigenmode space rather than directly in voxel/vertex space. Mathematical framework: Uses graph Fourier transform with random-walk Laplacian decomposition of structural connectivity. Models normative ranges on spectral coefficients and reconstructs arbitrary spatial queries through linear combinations. Includes sparse correlation structure modeling (threshold ρ=0.25) for cross-basis dependencies. Validation strategy is comprehensive: (1) reconstruction accuracy testing, (2) same-domain non-independent validation via training data analysis, (3) same-domain independent validation via 80-20 train-test split, and (4) different-domain validation via independent clinical cohort. Eigenmodes: Derived from high-resolution structural connectivity using MRtrix3 tractography (5 million streamlines) on fs-LR 32k template. Eigenmodes naturally extend across hemispheres while preserving neuroanatomical landmarks. Clinical sample note: MACC dataset acquired on different scanner (Siemens Magnetom Trio Tim) than training data (Siemens Skyra for HCP-YA, Siemens Prisma for HCP-A/D), demonstrating cross-scanner generalization. Fine-tuning used only 66 HC (50% of MACC HC cohort) to adapt site parameters. Preprint status: This is a medRxiv preprint dated January 21, 2025, not yet peer-reviewed. Code and model will be made available at a GitHub repository (link to be added). Study represents collaboration between National University of Singapore, University of Melbourne, Harvard Medical School, and University of Pennsylvania.
